messages:
lucas: quick RFC idea: a tiny manifest schema + two bot commands to reduce release note churn and make rollbacks trivial.

lucas: goals: single source of truth for pins, auto-generated release note template, change-window enforcement + safe rollback shortcuts.

priya: +1. what's the UX?

lucas: author a YAML manifest, run `rlsctl publish file.yaml` which validates, signs, uploads. then `release-bot apply --manifest-url=... --approve` kicks off the rollout. dry-run supported.

emma: sounds good. can manifest include a notes template so we don't paste the same bullets every time?

lucas: yep. example below. also include `changelog: auto` to let bot synthesize a two-line note, or `changelog: manual` to force copy.

lucas: ```yaml
# customer-hotfix-2026.yaml
version: 2026-04-01-01
services:
  - id: web-frontend
    target: 3.2.0
    strategy: blue-green
  - id: worker-embeddings
    target: 1.13.2-quant
    strategy: rolling
rollout:
  parallelism: 2
  pause_after: PT5M
  abort_on: [error_rate>0.02, latency_p90>200ms]
safety:
  change_window:
    start: 2026-04-02T02:00:00Z
    end: 2026-04-02T04:00:00Z
  lock_until: 2026-04-02T01:55:00Z
approvers:
  - @priya
  - @emma
changelog:
  mode: auto
  template: |
    - pinned {{services}} for customer ABC
    - expected impact: small CPU bump on worker-embeddings for first 10 minutes
notifications:
  on_failure: [#oncall, pagerduty]
  on_success: [#releases]
metadata:
  audit_tags: [customer:ABC, priority:high]
```

priya: I like `lock_until` to prevent accidental evening pushes. `pause_after` + `abort_on` helps automated guardrails.

emma: for rollbacks: `release-bot revert --service=web-frontend --to=3.1.9` or `release-bot revert --manifest-url=... --apply` would use manifest.rollback_to if present.

lucas: bot should keep a tiny per-service history (last 12 pins) to support `--to=recent` and `--to=previous`. Also attach an audit id to the manifest when published.

priya: infra: how do we ensure manifests aren't tampered with?

lucas: sign with an HMAC using a key in KMS, store signature in the manifest metadata and verify in bot before applying. stub: `rlsctl publish --sign` produces URL + sig.

emma: release notes automation: if `changelog.mode=auto` the bot expands `{{services}}` to a comma-separated list and emits a short note. It should also include the `approvers` and `audit_id`.

priya: can we add a `notes_template_vars` block so the bot can plug in recent perf deltas from Observability?

lucas: yes, manifest can have `notes_sources: [last_eval, perf_snapshot]` and `rlsctl` will attach snapshots.

ops-bot: Suggestion: require at least one approver from the manifest and a separate `release-team` ACL. I'll add a permission check to release-bot. :white_check_mark:

release-bot: publishing flow accepted. I'll add these flags: `--manifest-url`, `--signature`, `--dry-run`, `--hold-until`, `--annotate`. Will post a generated release note in channel and pin the manifest link.

emma: small UX ask: after apply, print `Summary: 2 services pinned · strategy: blue-green/rolling · lock_until: 2026-04-02T01:55Z · approvals: 2` and include a permalink to manifest + audit id.

lucas: and for emergency hotfixes, we need `--expedite --skip-lock` but gated to `release-admin` role.

priya: agreed. also add `--notify` to control notifications. by default notify on failures only.

lucas: last: template for quick revert message the bot posts: `Revert requested by @person for service X -> queued to rollout; next step: confirm apply with /confirm-revert` so humans can gate the revert when needed.

release-bot: I'll prototype a PoC this week. can we test on the staging change-window next Wed?

priya: tagging test plan: 1) publish+dry-run, 2) publish+apply in staging, 3) simulated failure triggers auto-abort, 4) revert flow. I'll open a checklist PR.

emma: thanks — ping in channel when PRs are up. :rocket:
